card: This PR fixes `interface_ipc*.py` test failures on NetBSD and adds CI enforcement to prevent similar regressions before merging. When IPC is enabled, socket and client connection reservations push bitcoind beyond NetBSD's 256 FD limit when paired with the test suite's default connection count, producing startup warnings that fail the tests. The PR subtracts IPC reservations from `-maxconnections` on IPC-enabled nodes and adds an `RLIMIT_NOFILE` wrapper to the macOS CI job to enforce the 256 FD limit on standard PR checks.
evidence: PR description links to failures on NetBSD: "This PR fixes the `interface_ipc*.py` tests, which have been failing on NetBSD since https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35037."

Commit 62571e7e67 notes: "Since -ipcbind reserves one listening socket plus ipc::DEFAULT_MAX_CONNECTIONS (16) client slots in min_required_fds, the framework's -maxconnections=76 no longer fits the 256 file descriptor budget on NetBSD, and every interface_ipc*.py node starts with 'Warning: Reducing -maxconnections ...', which the framework treats as a failure."
Author notes recurring regression pattern in PR description and commit 311bc7c3bb, citing prior fixes in PR #31537 and PR #36078 that were only caught post-merge by nightly NetBSD CI.
problem: On select()-based platforms like NetBSD, the total available file descriptors cannot exceed `FD_SETSIZE` (256). When `-ipcbind` was introduced, its 17 reserved file descriptors pushed the test framework's node startup requirements over 256, causing `bitcoind` to warn about reducing `-maxconnections`, which the test framework treats as a fatal test failure. Because NetBSD only runs in nightly CI, such FD budget regressions recur and go undetected in per-PR CI runs.

risk.why: Changes are strictly confined to test framework configuration and CI shell scripts.

summary: Fixes functional test failures in `interface_ipc*.py` on NetBSD by adjusting `-maxconnections` for nodes using IPC, and prevents future file descriptor budget regressions by adding an FD limit to the macOS CI task. Specifically, it lowers `-maxconnections` by 17 slots (one listening socket plus 16 client connections) when `-ipcbind` is enabled, and wraps node processes in the native macOS CI job with `ulimit -n 256` to mimic NetBSD's `FD_SETSIZE` constraint.
